$comment: Category explorer data. Edit this file to add/change taxonomy dimensions, their descriptions, and value summaries. Paper references for each value are computed automatically from papers.json (do not edit those).
intro: This page explains how the 53 reviewed papers were classified across the taxonomy of the systematic literature review. Each dimension below groups related categories; every category lists the papers that were classified with it. Click the arrow on a category to see its references.

dimensions.label: Research Type
dimensions.description: Describes whether the study's primary objective is to develop, extend, or evaluate XUQ methods (method-oriented) or to address a specific problem within a particular application domain using XUQ (application-oriented).

values.summary: XUQ is applied to address a specific problem within an application domain.
values.label: Application-oriented

values.summary: The study develops, extends, or evaluates XUQ methods.
values.label: Method-oriented

dimensions.label: Application Domain
dimensions.description: The real-world application domain in which XUQ is employed (for application-oriented studies).

dimensions.label: Data Modality
dimensions.description: The type of data the XUQ method operates on.

dimensions.label: ML Task
dimensions.description: Describes the ML task addressed by the study.

dimensions.label: Audience
dimensions.description: The intended target audience of the explanations, if mentioned.

values.summary: No target audience specified.

dimensions.label: Uncertainty Type
dimensions.description: The type of uncertainty that is explained.

values.summary: Overall predictive uncertainty (aleatoric + epistemic).
values.label: Predictive

values.summary: Uncertainty due to the model's lack of knowledge.
values.label: Epistemic

values.summary: Irreducible uncertainty inherent in the data.
values.label: Aleatoric

values.summary: Other uncertainty types.
values.label: Other

values.summary: The uncertainty type is not clearly specified in the paper.
values.label: Not specified

dimensions.label: UQ Method
dimensions.description: The method used to generate the uncertainty estimate.

values.summary: Uncertainty from disagreement across multiple model instances or stochastic inference runs (e.g., MC dropout, deep ensembles).
Uncertainty from explicitly modelling probability distributions over parameters or predictions (e.g., BNNs, Gaussian processes).
Uncertainty derived directly from the model's deterministic outputs, typically the softmax confidence or entropy.
Uncertainty quantified without parametric assumptions about the predictive distribution (e.g., conformal prediction, quantile regression).
Uncertainty based on the position or similarity of a sample within a learned representation space (e.g., VAEs).
Other or unspecified UQ methods.

dimensions.label: Uncertainty Estimate
dimensions.description: The specific uncertainty estimate that is explained.

values.summary: Uncertainty quantified as entropy of predictions.
Uncertainty quantified as variance or standard deviation.
Uncertainty quantified as prediction-interval widths or quantiles.
Uncertainty quantified as parameters of a fitted distribution.
Uncertainty quantified as probabilities or confidence scores.
Uncertainty quantified as distances in a representation or output space.
Other uncertainty estimates

dimensions.label: Integration Type
dimensions.description: Describes how the explanation is integrated with the model and the UQ mechanism

values.summary: Explanation applied after training, without changing the model.
Explanation retrieved directly from the model or UQ mechanism.
Combination of post-hoc and intrinsic elements.

dimensions.label: Portability
dimensions.description: Describes whether the XUQ method can be applied to any model or only to specific models or model classes.

values.summary: Applicable to any black-box model.
values.label: Model-agnostic

values.summary: Restricted to a specific model class or architecture.
values.label: Model-specific

dimensions.label: Locality
dimensions.description: Describes whether the explanation is specific to an instance or describes the overall model behaviour.

values.summary: Explanations specific to a single prediction.
values.label: Local

values.summary: Explanations of overall model behaviour.
values.label: Global

values.summary: Provides both local and global explanations.
values.label: Both

values.summary: Explanations that attribute uncertainty to individual input features.
values.label: Uncertainty attribution

values.summary: Explanations that describe which changes would alter the level of uncertainty.
Explanations that describe uncertainty in terms of higher-level concepts.
Explanations that describe uncertainty by logical rules or decision conditions.
Explanations that use representative examples or similar instances.
Other explanation output types.

dimensions.label: Evaluation conducted?
dimensions.description: Describes whether the explanations of uncertainty were evaluated in some form.

values.summary: The explanations were evaluated in some form.
The explanations were not evaluated.
Evaluation using quantitative proxy metrics.
Evaluation involving user studies with laypeople on simplified tasks.
Evaluation via anecdotal evidence as defined by Nauta et al. [1] ("showing individual, convincing examples that pass the first test of having face-validity").

dimensions.label: Co-12 Properties
dimensions.description: The Co-12 properties evaluated in a study as defined by Nauta et al. [1].

values.summary: Describes how faithful the explanation is w.r.t. the black box.
Describes how much of the black box behavior is described in the explanation.
Describes how deterministic and implementation-invariant the explanation method is.
Describes how continuous and generalizable the explanation function is.
Describes how discriminative the explanation is w.r.t. other events or targets.
Describes how complex the (interactions of) features in the explanation are.
Describes the size of the explanation.
Describes the presentation format and organization of the explanation.
Describes the presence and accuracy of probability information in the explanation.
Describes how relevant the explanation is to the user and their needs.
Describes how accordant the explanation is with prior knowledge and beliefs.
Describes how interactive or controllable an explanation is for a user.

dimensions.label: Benchmarked
dimensions.description: Describes whether the XUQ method was compared against other methods.

values.summary: The method was benchmarked against other approaches.
The method was not benchmarked.

dimensions.label: Attribution Detail
dimensions.description: For methods with uncertainty-attribution explanations, the specific attribution technique used.

values.summary: Attribution computed by perturbing inputs and observing changes in uncertainty.
Attribution computed from gradients of the uncertainty estimate.
Attribution based on counterfactual variations of the input.
Attribution computed with SHAP.
Other attribution techniques.
